activeResearch.title: Integrating Professional Dispositions in Nigerian Polytechnic Computing Education
activeResearch.description: As Principal Investigator, leading a TETFund-approved institutional research project to develop a framework for integrating professional dispositions into Nigerian polytechnic computing education. The study examines four dispositions — meticulousness, collaboration, self-directed learning, and persistence — through pre/post-surveys, structured learning activities, and reflective interventions among HND computing students. The research is informed by the ACM Computing Curricula 2020 (CC2020) competency framework. The project has an approved grant of ₦3.8 million, with one tranche disbursed to date.
activeResearch.status: Data collection, entry, and analysis complete · Manuscript in preparation for submission

activeResearch.title: International Impostor Phenomenon Study I
activeResearch.description: Led the Niger State Polytechnic site of an international multi-institutional study examining the impostor phenomenon among computing students. The international study was led by Prof. Leo Porter and Sophia Krause-Levy, in collaboration with partner institutions.
activeResearch.published: Conference paper presented at ACM CompEd 2025 (Best Paper Runner-Up); companion article published in ACM Transactions on Computing Education, 25(4), Article 47 (2025), receiving the 2026 Distinguished Paper Award.

activeResearch.title: International Impostor Phenomenon Study II
activeResearch.description: A second multi-institutional impostor phenomenon study led by Prof. Andrew Petersen of the University of Toronto Mississauga, with research instruments deployed through the Multi-Study Research Portal.
activeResearch.status: Ongoing · Data collection paused, with resumption planned when students return for the second semester at Niger State Polytechnic and partner institutions.

activeResearch.title: AlgoLadder — Bilingual Computational Thinking Tutor
activeResearch.description: A bilingual Hausa-English computational thinking tutor designed to support novice computing students who experience difficulties with introductory programming and computational thinking. The tutor is integrated into a multi-study research portal built with a Node.js/Express backend and Supabase PostgreSQL database.
activeResearch.status: Developed and deployed on the Multi-Study Research Portal · Participation of schools solicited · Awaiting second-semester resumption for data collection.
